facts.statement: The genus Scutarx was described by William G. Parker in 2016.
facts.quote: authority: Parker, 2016

facts.statement: Scutarx was a medium-sized, heavily armored reptile belonging to the herbivorous clade Aetosauria.
facts.quote: Scutarx is a medium-sized reptile with osteoderms belonging to the Aetosauria, a heavily armored and more herbivorous clade of pseudosuchians.

facts.statement: Scutarx is distinguished from other aetosaurs by a large, triangular boss on the dorsal surface of its osteoderms.
facts.quote: The presence of a large, triangular boss in the posteromedial corner of the dorsal surface of the dorsal paramedian osteoderms is the primary morphological characteristic that distinguishes Scutarx from other aetosaurs.

facts.statement: Fossils of Scutarx have been found in the Chinle Formation of Arizona and the Cooper Canyon Formation of Texas.
facts.quote: Fossils of Scutarx have been found in the Triassic Chinle Formation of Petrified Forest National Park of Arizona and the Cooper Canyon Formation of Texas.

facts.statement: Four partial skeletons of Scutarx, including the carapace and girdles, were collected between 2002 and 2009.
facts.quote: Four partial skeletons including much of the carapace, vertebral column as well as the shoulder and pelvic girdles have been collected from PEFO between 2002 and 2009.

facts.statement: Scutarx is classified within the family Stagonolepididae and the clade Aetosauriformes.
facts.quote: Scutarx belongs to the family Stagonolepididae of the clade Aetosauriformes.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis identifies Scutarx as the sister taxon to Adamanasuchus and Calyptosuchus within the clade Desmatosuchinae.
facts.quote: Scutarx deltatylus has been identified through phylogenetic analysis as the sister taxon of Adamanasuchus eisenhardtae and Calytosuchus wellesi, all forming a clade within Desmatosuchinae.

facts.statement: Scutarx measured between one and three meters in length and served as one of the earliest large herbivorous archosaurs of the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: Measuring between one and three meters in length, with strongly armored bodies and tails, it had a crucial ecological function of being the earliest and one of only two clades of big herbivorous archosaurs from the Late Triassic.

facts.statement: Unlike other aetosaurs, the frontal bone of Scutarx lacks a distinct, elevated midline ridge.
facts.quote: The distinct, elevated midline ridge that is found in other aertosaurs is however absent from the frontal of Scutarx.

facts.statement: A mid-trunk vertebra of Scutarx has a centrum that is 45.78 mm long and 41.81 mm tall.
facts.quote: The centrum has a ventral surface that is thin and smooth, profoundly concave lateral sides, and is longer (45.78 mm) than it is tall (41.81 mm).

facts.statement: The prezygapophyses of Scutarx vertebrae are inclined at approximately 45 degrees from the horizontal.
facts.quote: The prezygapophyses are inclined at around 45 degrees from the horizontal.

facts.statement: The neural spine of a Scutarx mid-trunk vertebra is 32.3 mm long, which is shorter than the centrum height.
facts.quote: In comparison to the centrum height, the neural spine is short (32.3 mm).

facts.statement: In posterior trunk vertebrae, the centra of Scutarx are taller than they are long.
facts.quote: The centra also become dorsoventrally taller than they are anteroposteriorly.

facts.statement: Scutarx possesses a robust sacral rib that extends laterally to touch the ilium.
facts.quote: A robust, wide sacral rib that laterally extends anterodorsally to touch the posterodorsal border of the left ilium is a recognizable feature of this element.

facts.statement: The anterior and mid-trunk ribs of Scutarx are double-headed.
facts.quote: The anterior and mid-trunk ribs are double-headed.

facts.statement: The pubis of Scutarx deltatylus uniquely features two large pubic foremen, a trait found in only one other aetosaur.
facts.quote: A unique character of the pubis of Scutarx deltatylus is the presence of two large pubic foremen, a characteristic seen in only one other aetosaur.

facts.statement: A distinctive triangular protuberance on the posteromedial corner of the osteoderms is used to identify Scutarx deltatylus.
facts.quote: The osteoderm's posteromedial corner contains the distinctive triangle protuberance used to identify Scutarx deltatylus.

facts.statement: The triangular protuberance on cervical osteoderms is shaped like a right triangle, unlike the equilateral triangles found in the trunk series.
facts.quote: In contrast to the equilateral triangles observed in the trunk series, the form of that protuberance is more like a right triangle in the cervical paramedian osteoderms.

facts.statement: Scutarx deltatylus lacks the "tongue-and-groove" lateral articular surfaces common in other aetosaurs.
facts.quote: The "tongue-and-groove" lateral articular surfaces found in other aetosaurias are absent in Scutarx deltatylus.

facts.statement: The scalloping of the anterior bar on Scutarx osteoderms is a shared characteristic found in all aetosaurs.
facts.quote: This "scalloping" of the anterior bar is a synapomorphy found in all aetosaurs.

facts.statement: Scutarx deltatylus was a herbivore, consistent with most other aetosaurs.
facts.quote: Scutarx deltatylus, like most aetosaurs however, was a herbivore.

facts.statement: Scutarx belongs to the parent group Desmatosuchinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Desmatosuchinae

facts.statement: Scutarx is classified in the family Stagonolepididae.
facts.quote: Family: Stagonolepididae

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Scutarx is Scutarx deltatylus.
facts.quote: Type species: Scutarx deltatylus

facts.statement: Scutarx lived during the Norian stage, from 227.3 to 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)
